channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Set for Rare APEC Trilateral Talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold a rare trilateral meeting Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Reporting from Shenzhen, Bloomberg’s Stephen Engle says that while the White House is framing the talks around denuclearization, the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran are likely to come up in discussions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman, Morgan Stanley Split on Yen Outlook on Diverging Forces
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are taking opposing views on the yen, highlighting the increasing difficulty in forecasting a currency being pulled in different directions.
item.dc:creator: John Cheng

item.title: IDR/USD: Indonesian Rupiah May Fall Further Past Record Low, Says Analysts
item.description: Indonesian authorities may struggle to put a floor under Asia’s worst-performing currency, according to strategists, as rising domestic political uncertainty and further capital outflows weigh on the rupiah.
item.dc:creator: Prima Wirayani

item.title: Australia Warns China Iron Ore Push Could Breach Trade Rules
item.description: Australia’s resources minister has expressed concern that state-backed buyer China Mineral Resources Group Co.’s negotiations with iron ore suppliers could breach international trade rules.
item.dc:creator: Paul-Alain Hunt

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 16
item.description: Oil steadied after a two-week slump, as fresh attacks in the Middle East countered signs of a well-supplied physical market.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Shenzhen’s Manufacturing Power Draws Wave of Innovators
item.description: You can't get the speed anywhere else": Despite tariffs and political narratives, hardware innovators from the US are rushing back to China's tech capital to turn their ideas into reality faster and cheaper.Bloomberg's Stephen Engle has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Philippines’ Main Coal Mine in Limbo Puts Nation’s Energy Supply at Risk
item.description: Sheila Potestad has spent two decades working as a welder at the Philippines’ largest coal mine on Semirara Island, on the western side of the archipelago. The mother of two is employed there alongside her husband. Now, more than 200 dump trucks, bulldozers and excavators are idle, seawater has forced a shutdown at one site, and the right to operate the mine is up for auction.
item.dc:creator: Cliff Venzon

item.title: US Futures Rebound After Two-Day Loss, Oil Slips: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equity-index futures rose in early Asian trading, pointing to a tentative recovery in market sentiment after a bout of weakness late last week. Oil slipped.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Burgess and Shikhar Balwani

item.title: Retail Crowd Dump Vietnam Stocks for Near 10% Bank-Deposit Rates
item.description: Vietnam’s retail investors are dumping equities and buying high-yielding notes from banks to capture interest rates nearing 10%, as locals and foreigners fall out of favor with the poor-performing stock market.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Kieu Giang

item.title: Diamondback in Talks to Buy Double Eagle for About $5 Billion
item.description: Diamondback Energy Inc. is in talks to acquire closely held oil driller Double Eagle V for about $5 billion, further expanding its position in the Permian Basin, the world’s most productive shale region, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: David Wethe

item.title: Pictet Adds Japan Stocks in Diversification Push After Midterms
item.description: Pictet Asset Management has added more Japanese shares to one of its multi-asset portfolios following the US midterm elections, in a bid to diversify and seek opportunities beyond stocks that are directly tied to artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Momoka Yokoyama

item.title: Roughed-Up Bond Traders Look to Fedspeak, Minutes for Next Move
item.description: Bond traders fresh off a bruising week will look to a slew of Federal Reserve speeches and the central bank’s most recent meeting minutes for clues on interest rates after the market ramped up expectations for an extended cycle of hikes.
item.dc:creator: Michael MacKenzie

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO Makes Dario Amodei the New Face of the AI Boom
item.description: The startup is set for the biggest IPO of all time, putting AI investors’ hopes and dreams — and fears — onto a frontier model maker.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz and Carmen Reinicke

item.title: Nvidia Fallout, Next Mega IPO, FAA Router Failure
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Fmr. TSA Administrator and Fmr. FBI Deputy Director John Pistole, Veda Partners Co-Founder and Director of Economic Policy Research Henrietta Treyz, Washington Post National Security Correspondent Tara Copp, “Embargo” Author and Journalist Philip Delves Broughton, PIMCO EVP, Market Strategist and Generalist Portfolio Manager Tony Crescenzi, Illinois Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Monument Advocacy Principal Mark Bednar. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Peru’s Economy Unexpectedly Slows as Mining, Farming Slump
item.description: Peru’s economy unexpectedly slowed in September, dragged down by weak mining and agriculture output.
item.dc:creator: Carla Samon Ros

item.title: Bookmarked: News Stories On Our Reading List
item.description: Foraging at luxury retreats, $20 million in cash found in Hungary, and the plight of big sisters: Join hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo on Bloomberg This Weekend for Bookmarked, where they share stories that caught their attention over the past week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: AI bots using credit cards, Meta and TikTok’s confidential payments to teens, how the wealthy are trying to keep kids at home, and a fundraising drunk raccoon: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House Braces for Democratic Investigations
item.description: Bully Pulpit International’s Adam Hodge and Monument Advocacy’s Mark Bednar are on Bloomberg This Weekend to examine the looming fight between congressional Democrats and the Trump administration over subpoenas, executive privilege and oversight of the White House’s relationships with corporate leaders. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they also discuss congressional scrutiny of Nvidia, the fallout from the FAA ground stop and where Republicans and Democrats could find room for bipartisan cooperation in the new Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inside India’s $130 Billion Wedding Economy
item.description: India’s weddings are a major economic force, generating an estimated $130 billion in annual spending.. For many families, the financial commitment begins years before the ceremony through savings and gold accumulation, while some households borrow against existing jewelry to finance wedding expenses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto’s Slow-Motion Selloff Leaves Traders Weary and Hopeless
item.description: Bitcoin’s latest selloff is testing the resolve of some of the cryptocurrency market’s most committed investors, as a succession of setbacks pushes prices toward their lowest levels of the year and major sources of demand weaken.
item.dc:creator: Muyao Shen
